customSections.label: Hawaii Calendar Notes — 2028–29
customSections.content: These details come from HIDOE’s official calendar page and the footnotes on the 2028–29 one-page calendar.

groups.label: Institute Day and converted planning days
items: One no-student Institute Day will fall during October 23–27, 2028; the exact date is determined by island.
Two instructional days are converted to non-student days for school planning and collaboration. HIDOE has not published fixed statewide dates for them.

groups.label: Teacher work year
items: HIDOE lists a 193-day teacher work year. Teachers report to campus for 189 days, while four additional days are converted to 27 hours: 21 hours for job-embedded professional development and six hours for training, planning, assessment, or teacher-evaluation meetings.

groups.label: Student days, return dates, and the senior schedule
items: The PDF shows 92 first-semester days and 90 second-semester days, then subtracts the two converted planning days for a total of 180 student days. HIDOE says Hawaii schools must provide 180 days totaling 1,080 hours.
Spring Break ends March 23, but March 26 is Prince Jonah Kūhiō Kalanianaʻole Day. Students return Tuesday, March 27.
The last day for seniors may be scheduled no earlier than May 10, 2029. That is a statewide threshold, not one senior last day or graduation date; individual schools publish their own schedules.

breakNotes.2028-12-22: Winter Break ends January 4. January 5 is a teacher workday, so students return Monday, January 8.
breakNotes.2029-03-19: Spring Break ends March 23. March 26 is Prince Jonah Kūhiō Kalanianaʻole Day, so students return Tuesday, March 27.

whatsNew.title: What Changed From 2027–28
whatsNew.subtitle: A concise comparison with the official 2027–28 HIDOE calendar.
content: The first student day moves from August 2 in 2027–28 to July 31 in 2028–29, while the last student day remains May 24.
Fall Break moves from October 4–8 to October 9–13; Winter Break moves from December 20–31 to December 22–January 4; and Spring Break moves from March 13–17 to March 19–23.
The Institute Day window moves from October 18–22 in 2027–28 to October 23–27 in 2028–29.
Election Day appears on the 2028–29 calendar on November 7, 2028; the 2027–28 calendar does not list an Election Day holiday.
The teacher work year begins July 25, two days earlier than the July 27 start in 2027–28.

calendarFaqs.q: Does the 2028–29 statewide calendar apply to every Hawaii public school?
calendarFaqs.a: HIDOE currently publishes the 2028–29 PDF as a future statewide school calendar. Its calendar page identifies Holomua Elementary and charter schools as exceptions for 2026–27 but does not repeat that statement under the future-year listing, so families at those schools should confirm their 2028–29 calendar directly.

calendarFaqs.q: What is the October 23–27 Institute Day window?
calendarFaqs.a: One no-student Educational Officer and Teacher Institute Day will occur during October 23–27, 2028. HIDOE does not publish one statewide date for it; the exact day is determined separately for each island.

calendarFaqs.q: Why do students return from Winter Break on January 8?
calendarFaqs.a: Winter Break ends January 4, but January 5 is a teacher workday with no students. January 6–7 is the weekend, so students return and begin the second semester on Monday, January 8.

calendarFaqs.q: Why does HIDOE have a 193-day teacher work year if teachers report to campus for 189 days?
calendarFaqs.a: HIDOE defines a 193-day teacher work year. Teachers report to campus for 189 days, while four additional days are converted to 27 hours for professional development, training, planning, assessment, or teacher-evaluation meetings.

calendarFaqs.q: What does ‘last day for seniors: no sooner than May 10’ mean?
calendarFaqs.a: HIDOE permits schools to schedule the last day for seniors on or after May 10, 2029. May 10 is the earliest allowed date, not one statewide senior last day or graduation date; individual schools publish their own schedules.

sourceReviewSummary: Official calendar approved May 15, 2025. MySchoolDates reviewed the current HIDOE calendar page and the complete 2028–29 PDF on August 20, 2026.
sourceReviewDetailsTitle: How the 2028–29 Hawaii calendar was checked
sourceReviewDetails: We reviewed the complete date grid, semester and quarter counts, state holidays, teacher work-year notes, and every footnote in the official PDF.
We also checked the HIDOE calendar page for the status of the future-year PDF and the 180-day/1,080-hour requirement.
Dates without a fixed statewide value, including Institute Day and two converted planning/collaboration days, are not represented as fixed dates in our ICS file.
sourceMaintainerText: The Hawaii State Department of Education publishes and revises the official statewide calendar.
